description: Number and expression display forms, typesetting wrappers (Superscript, Highlighted, Iconize), the box-level formatting system (Format, MakeBoxes, ToBoxes), grid layout options, session output variables (In, Out, $Pre, $Post) and modal dialogs for user interaction.

tools.name: PaddedForm
tools.description: Prints numbers padded to a fixed total width n (and f digits after the decimal point with {n, f}), so that columns of numbers align. Use it in tables, reports and fixed-width text export; options NumberPadding, NumberSigns and SignPadding control the padding characters.
tools.usage:
PaddedForm[expr, n]
PaddedForm[expr, {n, f}]
PaddedForm[expr, {n, f}, NumberPadding -> {" ", "0"}]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Digits to the right of the decimal point.

tools.notes: Formatting wrappers produce display objects; use ToString[PaddedForm[...]] or NumberForm with ToString to get plain strings.

tools.name: AccountingForm
tools.description: Prints numbers in accounting style: no scientific notation, negative numbers in parentheses, optional digit-block separators. Use it for financial tables.
tools.usage:
AccountingForm[expr]
AccountingForm[expr, n]
AccountingForm[expr, {n, f}, DigitBlock -> 3, NumberSeparator -> ","]

parameters.name: DigitBlock
parameters.description: Option: group digits in blocks of this size.

tools.name: EngineeringForm
tools.description: Prints real numbers in engineering notation, with exponents that are multiples of 3 (12.5 x 10^3). Use it for electrical and physical quantities where kilo/mega prefixes are natural.
tools.usage:
EngineeringForm[expr]
EngineeringForm[expr, n]

tools.name: DecimalForm
tools.description: Prints approximate real numbers in plain decimal notation without scientific exponents, with optional digit and decimal-place control. Use it when 1.*10^-7 style output is unwanted, e.g. in labels and reports.
tools.usage:
DecimalForm[expr]
DecimalForm[expr, n]
DecimalForm[expr, {n, f}]
tools.notes: Introduced in 12.0. PercentForm and NumberForm are related.

tools.name: PercentForm
tools.description: Prints a number as a percentage (0.253 displays as 25.3%), with optional digit control. Use it in dashboards and labels for ratios.
tools.usage:
PercentForm[expr]
PercentForm[expr, n]
PercentForm[expr, {n, f}]

tools.name: Short
tools.description: Prints a shortened version of an expression, showing at most n lines and replacing omitted parts with <<k>> skeletons. Use it to glance at large lists or results without flooding the notebook; Shallow instead limits depth and length.
tools.usage:
Short[expr]
Short[expr, n]
Shallow[expr]
Shallow[expr, {depth, length}]

parameters.name: {depth, length}
parameters.description: Shallow: maximum depth and elements per level (default {4, 10}).

tools.name: Superscript
tools.description: Superscript[x, y] displays x with superscript y purely as typesetting (no Power semantics); Subscript, Subsuperscript, Overscript, Underscript, OverBar and UnderBar are the companions. Use them for labels, units and index notation in plots and text.
tools.usage:
Superscript[x, y]
Subscript[x, y]
Subsuperscript[x, y, z]
Overscript[x, y]
Underscript[x, y]
OverBar[x]
UnderBar[x]
tools.example:
Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 10}, AxesLabel -> {Subscript["t", "s"], Superscript["v", "2"]}]
OverBar[x] (* x with a bar, e.g. a mean *)
tools.notes: Subscript[x, 1] is not a variable named x1; using it as a symbol in Solve or as an assignment target is a common source of confusion - prefer Symbol["x1"] or indexed variables x[1].

tools.name: Highlighted
tools.description: Displays an expression with a coloured background highlight (default yellow), optionally with a custom Background and RoundingRadius. Use it to emphasise results in reports and interactive interfaces.
tools.usage:
Highlighted[expr]
Highlighted[expr, Background -> color]
Highlighted[expr, effect]
tools.notes: Related wrappers: Framed, Underlined (13.x), Squiggled, Panel.

tools.name: Iconize
tools.description: Displays an expression as a compact icon (with a label) that still evaluates to the full expression; the notebook stores the complete data. Use it to embed large data, images or code in a notebook without visual clutter, e.g. when pasting data into a Manipulate.
tools.usage:
Iconize[expr]
Iconize[expr, "label"]
tools.notes: Introduced in 11.3. The iconized form stays a valid input expression when copied.

tools.name: Format
tools.description: Format[expr] = display defines how expr (typically a custom head) is printed in all output forms, while Format[expr, TraditionalForm] etc. restrict to one form. It is the simplest way to give your own data structures a readable summary display; MakeBoxes is the lower-level alternative.
tools.usage:
Format[f[args___]] := display
Format[f[x_], TraditionalForm] := ...
Format[expr, form]
tools.example:
Format[vec[x_, y_]] := Row[{"<", x, ", ", y, ">"}]
vec[1, 2] (* prints as <1, 2> but FullForm is vec[1, 2] *)
tools.notes: Formatting rules do not affect evaluation or InputForm. Use Interpretation when the display should also be copyable.

tools.name: MakeBoxes
tools.description: The low-level typesetting hook: MakeBoxes[expr, form] gives the box structure (RowBox, SuperscriptBox, GridBox, ...) used by the front end to display expr. Defining MakeBoxes rules for a head gives complete control over its display; MakeExpression is the inverse (boxes to expression) used when input is parsed.
tools.usage:
MakeBoxes[expr, StandardForm]
MakeBoxes[f[x_], StandardForm] := RowBox[{"f(", MakeBoxes[x, StandardForm], ")"}]
MakeExpression[boxes, StandardForm]
tools.example:
MakeBoxes[pt[x_, y_], StandardForm] ^:= RowBox[{"(", MakeBoxes[x, StandardForm], ",", MakeBoxes[y, StandardForm], ")"}]
pt[1, 2]
ToBoxes[a^2 + b] // FullForm
tools.notes: Use UpSetDelayed (^:=) so the rule attaches to your symbol rather than to MakeBoxes. Prefer Format unless box-level control is needed.

tools.name: ToBoxes
tools.description: Converts an expression to its box representation (the typeset form the front end draws); RawBoxes wraps boxes so they display literally, and DisplayForm renders boxes as they would appear. Use these when generating typeset content programmatically or exporting to other typesetting systems.
tools.usage:
ToBoxes[expr]
ToBoxes[expr, form]
RawBoxes[boxes]
DisplayForm[boxes]

tools.name: StandardForm
tools.description: The default two-dimensional output form of notebooks (also valid input); OutputForm is the one-dimensional text form used by wolframscript and Print in terminals; TraditionalForm mimics textbook notation; MathMLForm and FortranForm give MathML and Fortran output. Wrap an expression in a form to display it that way, or use Export/ExportString with the corresponding format.
tools.usage:
StandardForm[expr]
OutputForm[expr]
MathMLForm[expr]
FortranForm[expr]
SetOptions[$Output, FormatType -> OutputForm]
tools.example:
OutputForm[Integrate[1/(1 + x^3), x]]
FortranForm[x^2 + Sin[y]] (* x**2 + Sin(y) *)
ExportString[Sqrt[x], "MathML"]
tools.notes: ToString[expr, form] converts any form to a string, e.g. ToString[expr, TeXForm].

tools.name: Spacer
tools.description: Inserts horizontal (or {w, h}) blank space in Row, Column, Grid and graphics Inset layouts; Invisible[expr] takes the space of expr without drawing it. Use them for fine alignment in custom interfaces and legends.
tools.usage:
Spacer[w]
Spacer[{w, h}]
Invisible[expr]

tools.name: Magnify
tools.description: Displays an expression magnified by a factor (default 1.5) without changing font settings, and Deploy makes an interactive object non-editable (controls still work). Both are display wrappers useful for presentations and delivered interfaces.
tools.usage:
Magnify[expr]
Magnify[expr, r]
Deploy[expr]

tools.name: Item
tools.description: Item[expr, opts] wraps a single entry of Grid, Column, Row, Menu-like constructs or Multicolumn to give it its own Background, Alignment, Frame, ItemSize or Style. SpanFromLeft, SpanFromAbove and SpanFromBoth mark cells that merge with their neighbours.
tools.usage:
Item[expr, Background -> color, Alignment -> Right]
Grid[{{"a", SpanFromLeft}, {"b", "c"}}]
tools.example: Grid[{{Item["Header", Background -> LightGray], SpanFromLeft}, {1, 2}}, Frame -> All]

tools.name: Dividers
tools.description: Option for Grid, Column, Row and Multicolumn specifying where divider lines go (None, All, Center, or {x-spec, y-spec} with explicit indices and styles). Alignment, Spacings, ItemSize and ItemStyle are the other core grid layout options; Frame -> All gives a full border.
tools.usage:
Grid[data, Dividers -> All]
Grid[data, Dividers -> {False, {2 -> True}}]
Grid[data, Alignment -> {{Left, Right}, Center}, Spacings -> {2, 1}, ItemSize -> {8, 1.5}]

parameters.name: Dividers
parameters.description: None, All, Center, or {columnspec, rowspec} with positions -> style.

parameters.name: ItemSize
parameters.description: Width/height of items in ems/lines; Full to fill.

tools.example: Grid[Prepend[data, {"x", "y"}], Dividers -> {False, {2 -> Black}}, Alignment -> Right, ItemSize -> 6]

tools.name: Multicolumn
tools.description: Lays out a flat list in n columns (filling column by column by default, or row by row with Appearance settings), an easy alternative to Grid[Partition[...]] for long lists of items such as thumbnails or names.
tools.usage:
Multicolumn[list, n]
Multicolumn[list, {Automatic, m}]
Multicolumn[list, n, Appearance -> "Horizontal"]

tools.name: In
tools.description: In[n] and Out[n] hold the n-th input and output of the session; % is Out[$Line - 1], %% the one before and %n is Out[n]. $Line is the current line number. Use them interactively; avoid in scripts and packages where they make code non-reproducible.
tools.usage:
In[n]
Out[n]
%
%%
%n
$Line
tools.example:
Expand[(x + 1)^3]
D[%, x]
Out[1] === In[1] (* False *)
Clear[Out] (* free memory held by old outputs *)
tools.notes: $HistoryLength controls how many outputs are retained; set it to 0 in memory-hungry sessions.

tools.name: $Pre
tools.description: Session hooks: $Pre is applied to every input before evaluation, $Post to every output, $PrePrint to every output before printing (e.g. to abbreviate or reformat), and $PreRead to the raw input string/boxes. Use them for global logging, automatic Short display or timing of all evaluations.
tools.usage:
$Pre = f
$Post = f
$PrePrint = f
$PreRead = f
tools.notes: These have attribute-free assignment semantics; set to . (Unset) to remove. $Pre must have HoldAll-like behaviour to see unevaluated input: $Pre = Function[x, ..., HoldAll].

tools.name: ChoiceDialog
tools.description: Opens a modal dialog asking a question and returns the value of the chosen button (True/False for the default OK/Cancel, or from a list of label -> value choices). Use it for confirmations in interactive tools.
tools.usage:
ChoiceDialog[expr]
ChoiceDialog[expr, {lbl1 -> val1, lbl2 -> val2, ...}]
ChoiceDialog[expr, choices, opts]
tools.example:
If[ChoiceDialog["Overwrite existing file?"], Export[file, data]]
mode = ChoiceDialog["Pick a mode", {"Fast" -> 1, "Accurate" -> 2}]
tools.notes: Blocks the kernel until the user answers; not usable in headless wolframscript runs.

tools.name: DialogInput
tools.description: Opens a modal dialog window containing arbitrary controls and returns the value passed to DialogReturn[value] when the user finishes. Form-like shortcuts accept a list of variable -> control specifications. Use it for custom parameter-entry dialogs.
tools.usage:
DialogInput[expr]
DialogInput[{x -> x0, ...}, body]
DialogInput[DynamicModule[{...}, Column[{..., DefaultButton[DialogReturn[value]], CancelButton[]}]]]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Dialog contents; must call DialogReturn to finish.

tools.example:
params = DialogInput[DynamicModule[{n = 10, tol = 0.01},
   Column[{Row[{"n: ", InputField[Dynamic[n], Number]}],
           Row[{"tol: ", InputField[Dynamic[tol], Number]}],
           Row[{DefaultButton[DialogReturn[{n, tol}]], CancelButton[DialogReturn[$Canceled]]}]}]]]
tools.notes: CreateDialog opens a non-modal dialog window instead; SystemDialogInput opens native OS dialogs (file open/save, colour, directory).

tools.name: SystemDialogInput
tools.description: Opens a native operating-system dialog: "FileOpen", "FileSave", "Directory", "Color", "RecordSound" and returns the chosen path/value or $Canceled. Use it to let users pick files and folders in notebook tools.
tools.usage:
SystemDialogInput["FileOpen"]
SystemDialogInput["FileSave", "default.csv"]
SystemDialogInput["Directory"]
SystemDialogInput["Color"]

parameters.name: init
parameters.description: Initial path, file name or value; for file dialogs {path, {"Label" -> {"*.csv"}}} adds filters.

tools.example:
file = SystemDialogInput["FileOpen", {$HomeDirectory, {"Data files" -> {"*.csv", "*.xlsx"}}}];
If[file =!= $Canceled, data = Import[file]]

tools.name: CreateDialog
tools.description: Creates a non-modal dialog notebook window containing the given expression (typically a DynamicModule with controls); returns a NotebookObject that can be closed with NotebookClose or DialogReturn. Use it for floating tool windows and palettes that do not block evaluation.
tools.usage:
CreateDialog[expr]
CreateDialog[expr, WindowTitle -> "title", Modal -> True]

parameters.name: Modal
parameters.description: Option: True blocks the front end until closed.

tools.example: dlg = CreateDialog[Column[{"Monitoring", Dynamic[status], Button["Close", DialogReturn[]]}], WindowTitle -> "Status"]
tools.notes: CreatePalette creates a palette-style window; CreateWindow a general notebook window.

tools.name: ProgressIndicator
tools.description: Displays a progress bar for a value in a range, or an indeterminate/necklace animation when the value is unknown. Combine with Dynamic or Monitor to show computation progress; StatusArea shows a message in the window status bar on mouseover.
tools.usage:
ProgressIndicator[Dynamic[x]]
ProgressIndicator[Dynamic[x], {min, max}]
ProgressIndicator[Appearance -> "Indeterminate"]
StatusArea[expr, "status text"]

tools.name: Hyperlink
tools.description: Creates a clickable link that opens a URL, a file, a notebook or a documentation page; Hyperlink[label, uri] shows a custom label. Use it in generated reports and interfaces; in exported HTML it becomes an anchor.
tools.usage:
Hyperlink[uri]
Hyperlink[label, uri]
Hyperlink[label, {nb, "CellTag"}]

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: URL, file path, or "paclet:ref/Plot" documentation link.

tools.name: ClickToCopy
tools.description: Displays an expression that, when clicked, copies it (or a specified expression) to the clipboard; PasteButton inserts an expression into the notebook at the current selection when clicked. Useful in generated code snippets and palettes.
tools.usage:
ClickToCopy[expr]
ClickToCopy[label, expr]
PasteButton[expr]
PasteButton[label, expr]
tools.example:
ClickToCopy["copy the API key", apiKey]
PasteButton["Insert template", Defer[Plot[f[x], {x, 0, 1}]]]

tools.name: PopupWindow
tools.description: Wraps an expression so that clicking it opens a separate window displaying another expression; useful for drill-down details and large tooltips that need scrolling. The window closes when the user clicks away or explicitly.
tools.usage:
PopupWindow[expr, contents]
PopupWindow[expr, contents, WindowSize -> {w, h}]

tools.name: Underlined
tools.description: Displays an expression with an underline, as a simple text decoration wrapper (the companion of Highlighted and Squiggled, and equivalent to Style[expr, Underlined] for text).
tools.usage:
Underlined[expr]
Style[expr, Underlined]

tools.name: Skeleton
tools.description: Skeleton[n] represents n omitted elements in an expression printed with Short (shown as <<n>>); TotalWidth and PageWidth control line wrapping of printed output. Recognising Skeleton lets code detect abbreviated output and PageWidth -> Infinity prevents wrapping in exported text.
tools.usage:
Skeleton[n]
SetOptions[$Output, PageWidth -> Infinity]
ToString[expr, PageWidth -> Infinity]

parameters.name: PageWidth
parameters.description: Option of streams and ToString: characters per line.

tools.example:
Short[Range[100]] (* {1, 2, <<96>>, 99, 100} *)
WriteString[stream, ToString[longExpr, InputForm, PageWidth -> Infinity]]

tools.name: Annotation
tools.description: Annotation[expr, tag] attaches invisible metadata to an expression; in graphics, tags of type "Mouse", "Tooltip" or a plain symbol can be read back by AnnotationValue or used by EventHandler. Use it to tag graphics elements for interactive selection.
tools.usage:
Annotation[expr, tag]
Annotation[expr, tag, type]
AnnotationValue[obj, key]

tools.name: TextCell
tools.description: TextCell["text", "Style"] and ExpressionCell[expr, "Style"] build Cell expressions from strings or expressions without hand-writing BoxData/TextData; use them with CellPrint, NotebookWrite and CreateDocument to generate notebooks programmatically.
tools.usage:
TextCell["text"]
TextCell["text", "Section"]
ExpressionCell[expr, "Input"]
ExpressionCell[expr, "Output", opts]

tools.name: BoxData
tools.description: The low-level content wrappers inside Cell expressions: BoxData holds typeset boxes (RowBox, SuperscriptBox, GridBox, StyleBox...), TextData holds text with inline boxes, and CellGroupData groups cells (with an Open/Closed state). Needed when reading notebook expressions with NotebookGet/NotebookRead or writing them manually.
tools.usage:
Cell[BoxData[boxes], "Input"]
Cell[TextData[{"text", Cell[BoxData[...]]}], "Text"]
Cell[CellGroupData[{cell1, cell2, ...}, Open]]
tools.example:
nb = NotebookGet[EvaluationNotebook[]];
Cases[nb, Cell[BoxData[b_], "Input", ___] :> ToExpression[b, StandardForm, Hold], Infinity]

tools.name: QuantityForm
tools.description: Controls how Quantity objects are displayed: unit abbreviations, long names, singular/plural forms, and whether the unit is shown, without changing the value. Use it for report formatting of physical quantities.
tools.usage:
QuantityForm[q, "Abbreviation"]
QuantityForm[q, "LongForm"]
QuantityForm[q, {"Magnitude", "Unit"}]

tools.name: SwatchLegend
tools.description: SwatchLegend, LineLegend and PointLegend build standalone legend objects (coloured swatches, line samples or markers with labels) that can be attached to any expression with Legended[expr, legend] or placed via Placed[legend, pos]; they are also what PlotLegends produces internally. Use them to build shared legends for GraphicsGrid layouts or custom Graphics.
tools.usage:
SwatchLegend[{c1, c2, ...}, {"lbl1", "lbl2", ...}]
LineLegend[{c1, c2, ...}, {"lbl1", ...}]
PointLegend[{c1, c2, ...}, {"lbl1", ...}]
Legended[expr, Placed[legend, Below]]
tools.example: Legended[Graphics[{Red, Disk[], Blue, Disk[{2, 0}]}], SwatchLegend[{Red, Blue}, {"A", "B"}]]
tools.notes: Options LegendLayout ("Row"/"Column"), LegendMarkers, LegendLabel and LegendFunction customise appearance. The PlotLegends option itself is covered in the plot options chunk.

tools.name: Squiggled
tools.description: Displays an expression with a squiggly underline (the spell-check style), a decorative wrapper in the same family as Highlighted and Underlined; useful for marking questionable values in generated reports.
tools.usage:
Squiggled[expr]
Squiggled[expr, color]

tools.name: NumberFormat
tools.description: Option of NumberForm, ScientificForm and friends giving a function that receives the mantissa, base and exponent strings and returns the display, enabling custom notations (e.g. 1.5e3 or 1.5×10^3 with a different font). Related options: NumberPadding, NumberSigns, NumberPoint, ExponentFunction, DigitBlock, NumberSeparator.
tools.usage:
NumberForm[x, n, NumberFormat -> (Row[{#1, "e", #3}] &)]
NumberForm[x, ExponentFunction -> (Null &)]

parameters.name: ExponentFunction
parameters.description: Function deciding which exponent to display (Null & suppresses exponents).

parameters.name: NumberPoint
parameters.description: Decimal point string, e.g. "," for European style.

tools.example:
NumberForm[1.5*^-7, NumberFormat -> (Row[{#1, "e", #3}] &)] (* 1.5e-7 *)
NumberForm[12345.678, DigitBlock -> 3, NumberSeparator -> ".", NumberPoint -> ","]
